stories.title: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district
summary: An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.
Under the Makkah Defence Alliance, Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish leaders met in Riyadh and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.
The fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.

stories.title: By-polls in Gujranwala's NA-77, Sahiwal's PP-203 conclude
summary: Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja also visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) said.
On Saturday, the ECP took notice of an alleged violation of the Code of Conduct by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar during by-election campaigning in NA-77.
Subsequently, the ECP scheduled a by-election for Nov 23, 2025, which was won by Jutt with 46,820 votes.

stories.title: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of counterterrorism initiatives
summary: Chairing his first apex committee meeting after taking charge of the province, governor Kundi promised to equip police and CTD with resources. “Whatever weapons you want, whatever you need, we will get them to you.

Governor Kundi calls for ownership of war against terrorism Speaking at the occasion, Governor Kundi said the provincial government’s priority was to restore peace and strengthen the police force, stressing that development would follow once security was ensured.

He said the police were at the forefront of the war against terrorism and needed to be adequately equipped to carry out their responsibilities. “Until we strengthen and facilitate [the police], how will they fight using just one Kalashnikov and a few bullets?” Kundi asked.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz, Nawaz discuss ‘matters of national importance’ as Sharifs gather at Lahore's Jati Umra
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif discussed matters of “national importance” with PML-N President Nawaz Sharif during a visit to the latter’s residence in Lahore’s Jati Umra on Sunday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.
PM Shehbaz briefed the PML-N president on the law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and on recent initiatives taken for the development and prosperity of the province, Radio Pakistan added.
The premier also apprised Nawaz of “the ongoing economic reforms by the government, the challenges being faced and the measures being taken to address them”, the outlet said.

stories.title: Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten century guides Pakistan U-19 to thrilling win over India
summary: Hamza Zahoor produced a match-winning unbeaten century as Pakistan Under-19 defeated arch-rivals India by three wickets in a thrilling Group ‘A’ encounter of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Sunday.
Pakistan’s chase, however, was far from straightforward as India’s bowlers made early inroads to reduce them to 61 for five.
However, the right-hander received little support from the other end as Pakistan’s bowlers maintained pressure and regularly picked up wickets to restrict India to a modest total.

stories.title: SAFF Championship: Pakistan cruise past Maldives 3-0, close in on semi-final spot
summary: A first-half brace from Najeebullah Bettani, alongside an early penalty converted by McKeal Aroon Abdullah, helped Pakistan register their first victory of the tournament and put themselves in a strong position to qualify for the last four.

With their victory over Maldives, Pakistan have moved into a stronger position in the qualification race but must now wait for the outcome of the remaining Group ‘B’ fixture between India and Maldives, scheduled for Nov 11.
Maldives will need a substantial victory over India to overtake Pakistan in the group standings and secure qualification.

stories.title: 'Misplaced over-smartness': Maryam removes Jhelum DC over exam postponement for her visit
summary: Originally scheduled for Nov 10, the computer science papers for the Intermediate Second Annual Examinations 2026 had been deferred on the recommendation of the now-dismissed Jhelum DC, Mir Raza Ozgen.

It is, therefore, requested that the examination be postponed and rescheduled for another suitable date to avoid any inconvenience to students and ensure the smooth conduct of both the examination and the VVIP visit”.

stories.title: ‘Special connection with Pakistan’: US Senator Van Hollen, eyeing 2028 presidential bid, was born in Karachi
summary: US Democrat Senator Christopher Van Hollen, who has set his sights on the 2028 contest for the American presidential office, was born in Karachi.

I am fortunate to have a special connection with Pakistan, having been born in Karachi as the son of an American foreign service officer. “Throughout my life, I have experienced first-hand the generosity, the goodness and the determination of the Pakistani people.
In 2021, Van Hollen had thanked Pakistan among other countries for helping evacuate American nationals and others stranded in Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover of the country.

stories.title: Pakistan-built robots serve taste of future to Karachi diners
summary: Restaurant staff say the novelty has brought a surge in customers — some travelling from across the sprawling port city to meet the robots.

stories.title: RETHINKING PAKISTAN’S AUTO POLICY
summary: An auto policy cannot run provincial bus services, but it can reduce fleet costs and make public support conditional on affordable service.

Under these assumptions, monthly costs per commuter are roughly Rs1,900 for a bus, Rs4,900 for an electric motorcycle, Rs5,200 for wagons and rickshaws, Rs7,000 for a petrol motorcycle and Rs39,900 for a small petrol car.
In my model, an electric bus running around 70,000 kilometres a year with 800 passenger boardings a day needs about Rs21.5 million in annual public support if borrowing costs 18 percent.

stories.title: Pakistan edge India, enter semis
summary: Hamza Zahoor struck an unbeaten century to guide Pakistan Under-19s to a thrilling three-wicket victory over India and secure their place in the semi-finals of the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) Under-19 Asia Cup on Sunday.
Chasing 209 at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman, Pakistan achieved the target with 11 balls to spare with Zahoor producing a match-winning 100 not out off 108 deliveries to steer his side home.
Rajput held India's innings together despite losing partners at the other end, but Pakistan's bowlers kept striking to prevent the visitors from building a bigger total.

stories.title: Can't cook or shower: Indonesians take aim at data centres

stories.title: Pakistan whip Maldives to stay alive
summary: Pakistan moved closer to securing a place in the semi-finals after producing a dominant 3-0 victory over Maldives in their second Group B match of the SAFF Cup at National Stadium Dhaka on Sunday.

Collecting a clearance on the right after Pakistan had defended deep in their own half, Bettani brought the ball under control before unleashing a powerful strike beyond the helpless Maldives goalkeeper.
Pakistan must now await the outcome of the remaining Group match between the Maldives and India to confirm their semi-final qualification.

stories.title: Babar Azam says selection not in his hands as youthful Pakistan face Sri Lanka
summary: Babar’s remarks come as Pakistan prepare to field a considerably revamped side following their disappointing performance in the previous phase of the World Test Championship (WTC).

The hosts defeated Sri Lanka in the final of the ODI tri-series towards the end of October, and Babar believes the result has helped lift the team’s confidence. “Any series or match you win gives you confidence, and we have brought that vibe into the Test matches.

stories.title: Electric auto rickshaws reshape India's roads
summary: Every 90 seconds, an electric three-wheeler rolls off the production line at an Indian factory, underscoring a transformation that has made the country the largest market for battery-powered auto rickshaws.
"Rickshaws, which operate continuously throughout the day, accumulate fuel savings rapidly," said Bidisha Bhattacharya of the Delhi-based Chintan Research Foundation.
Climate think-tank Ember said India consumes less transport fuel per capita than China did at a comparable income level in 2012, helped by the spread of cheap solar power and declining battery costs.

stories.title: Democrats planning flood of AI bills when they take control of Congress
summary: Democrats are planning to unleash a flood of new legislation targeting artificial intelligence systems and data-center development when they take control of the US Congress in January, lawmakers, congressional aides and advocates said.

Democrats plan on introducing bills aimed at shielding consumers from rising electricity costs tied to data centers, requiring independent testing of advanced AI systems and clarifying when AI companies can be held liable for harm caused by their products, they said.

Most US voters think ​Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new ​regulations for the technology, ⁠according to a Reuters poll published in October.

stories.title: Trump orders US Justice Department to look into Democrats for 'threatening' people with impeachment, other penalties

stories.title: Hodge ton puts West Indies in command against Bangladesh
summary: Kavem Hodge hit an unbeaten 140 to extend West Indies' lead to 315 on the fourth day of the second Test against Bangladesh in Sylhet on Sunday.
West Indies reached 345-3 in their second innings when bad light halted play, with Hodge hitting 17 fours and a six off 189 balls and Amir Jangoo also unbeaten on 20.
Hodge said he was pleased to contribute after failing to convert a start in the first Test in Dhaka, adding that the West Indies would assess conditions before deciding when to declare.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz briefs Nawaz Sharif on K-P security, economic challenges

stories.title: Usman Khawaja denies throwing 'anyone under the bus' with comments about Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal
summary: Usman Khawaja insisted on Sunday he did not “throw anyone under the bus” by claiming the entire Australian team was in on the 2018 “Sandpapergate” plot and defended taking eight years to go public.

That probe found only Smith, Warner and Bancroft were in the know. “When I mentioned it was all of us, that’s implying that whether we like it or not, we’re all responsible for what happened together as a team,” Khawaja said in a lengthy Instagram post on Sunday.

That’s the first time I tried to come out.” Khawaja said he again almost spoke up in 2021 when bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly that they knew about the ball-tampering.

stories.title: Bomb Disposal Squad official martyred as IED goes off in KP's South Waziristan
summary: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: An assistant head of the police’s Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS) was martyred after an improvised explosive device (IED) went off in the Janta area of Sararogha tehsil in Upper South Waziristan district on Saturday while he was attempting to defuse it.

Upper South Waziristan district police officer (DPO) Ashfaq Khan told Dawn that the official, identified as Abdul Jabbar, was busy defusing the IED when an explosion occurred, leaving him seriously injured.

On the same day, an incident was reported in Toi Khulla Bazaar in Lower South Waziristan district, where an unidentified person wearing a burqa threw a hand grenade near the place where police personnel were seated.

stories.title: Poland mourns victims of Krakow mass shooting as security fears grow
summary: Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, and police ​bolstered security after six people were killed in a mass shooting in Krakow that authorities said was likely ‌inspired by far-right ideology.
Streets closed as mourners leave candles In Krakow, the old town's main market square and the ​surrounding streets remained closed, with police allowing only essential workers to pass.

stories.title: PTI's Gohar demands end to ‘political victimisation’
summary: SWAT: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Saturday called for judicial independence, rule of law and an end to what he described as political victimisation.
The PTI chairman said that access to party founder Imran Khan, including meetings with his personal physician and family members, remained their foremost demand.
Describing political isolation and what he termed “political apartheid” as harmful to democracy, Barrister Khan expressed concern over the alleged illegal detention of political leaders.

stories.title: Governor invites Chinese investors to explore KP’s potential
summary: The meeting, attended by a delegation of Chinese investors, focused on investment opportunities in the province, particularly in the minerals sector, as well as the potential for investment in its economic zones, according to a statement issued by the governor’s office.

stories.title: ECC grant for aircraft maintenance not new luxury jet, officials clarify
summary: The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) has not approved Rs1.094 billion for the purchase of a new luxury executive jet for the military leadership, contrary to claims circulating on social media, officials have clarified.

According to ECC sources and Ministry of Defence (MoD) officials, the allocation is exclusively meant for the maintenance, operational overhaul and induction-related logistics of an existing aircraft currently being used by the prime minister.

The clarification comes amid social media claims that the government had sanctioned funds for the procurement of a high-end executive aircraft, such as the Embraer Lineage 1000, for military leadership.

stories.title: Karachi SHO suspended after audio of apology to drug dealer surfaces
summary: KARACHI: The station house officer (SHO) of the Pak Colony police station was suspended after an audio clip went viral on social media in which he purportedly sought an apology from a drug dealer.

According to an order, an audio recording surfaced on social media on Nov 5, allegedly featuring the SHO and a police constable in an “unauthorised, compromising conversation with a known drug peddler, Kashif alias Dada”.
The SHO had “compromised the writ of law” by pursuing mutual reconciliation with a criminal and directing his subordinate to apologise to the drug peddler, the order stated.

stories.title: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority plans to challenge court order over Bari Imam House
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority has decided to challenge the Islamabad High Court’s interim order that directed it to de-seal Bari Imam House.
The IHC had on November 3 directed the CDA and other respondents to “forthwith de-seal the premises” and barred any further demolition until the next hearing.

The CDA, which sealed the premises on October 30 in a joint operation with the district administration, claimed the structure stands on government land and was among properties identified for action under its anti-encroachment drive.

stories.title: ‘No suitable candidate’ among nearly 100 applicants for Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research's top post
summary: Under Section 4(1)(a) read with Section 5(1) of the PCSIR Act, 1973, the ministry has proposed that Dr Abidi be re-nominated for a further period of one year – from October 19, 2026, to October 18, 2027 – or until a regular chairman is appointed, whichever is earlier.
Dr Abidi had initially been appointed as the PCSIR chairman on October 19, 2020, for a standard three-year term.

As per the standard practices, the ministry notifies committees for the scrutiny and selection of a suitable candidate for the post; however, no committee was notified following receipt of the applications, the sources alleged.

stories.title: Karachi sees sharp rise in ‘encounter’ killings as 200 shot dead in 10 months
summary: The data maintained by Karachi police shows that besides killing 197 suspects, police encounters left 1,426 others wounded — a 67.9pc rise from 849 arrested in wounded condition during the same period last year.
